rubrics.criterion: The component that forms tokens holds only the program material it actually tokenizes (the prepared lines used by the token loop), and no longer carries a parallel staged copy of the raw program text, nor a stored source location, as state that nothing in tokenization reads.
rubrics.rationale: The maintainer's report specifically calls out that loading got reshaped into staged raw material plus an origin record held alongside the tokenizing contents; dissolving that double-keeping is the ingestion half of this instance, in whatever shape the repair takes.

rubrics.criterion: Word-spelling corrections resolve through the packaged language vocabulary as a single shared mechanism (the existing alias-then-pattern behavior), with no per-run copy of the correction table seeded onto, or maintained by, the token-forming component.
rubrics.rationale: The instance's vocabulary duty is specifically a copy-on-instance of an already-shared table shadowing the shared lookup; the case is resolved when corrections read the shared language data again from wherever corrections are decided, not merely when the copy is renamed or moved.

rubrics.criterion: The required program opening and closing words are enforced from language-level constants or ordinary local rules at the place where program shape is validated, and are no longer carried as a dedicated per-object record on the token-forming component with helpers that exist only to service that record.
rubrics.rationale: The report names the marker words being promoted into an object-held protocol record with dedicated helper methods as one of the accumulated jobs; whether the enforcement stays at analysis time or moves, the outcome is that the language rule is read from shared or local rule data rather than instance configuration.

rubrics.criterion: The token-forming component has no role in producing the two debug evidence files: the dump trigger condition, the destination-path derivation, and the file writing are all located outside it, in the layer that runs the pipeline or in a component whose concern is reporting.
rubrics.rationale: Debug report authorship is the duty this case moved in from the pipeline driver, including its trigger flag and path bookkeeping; its removal from the token-forming component is the largest and most clearly stated half of the requested ownership restoration in this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely redistribute the centralization: after it, no single owner (and no small set of two or three owners) still each holds several of the previously consolidated job groups — tokenization together with ingestion staging, correction records, marker records, or report bookkeeping — instead of each group having its own focused home.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible failure for this task is a cosmetic shuffle: renaming the instance records, splitting the big class into two medium ones, or wrapping the same mixture in a facade, all of which leave the maintainer reading loading, vocabulary, protocol and report code to touch a keyword — the exact complaint that motivated this task.

rubrics.criterion: The pipeline driver is rewired consistently with the new ownership: it obtains the token stream and parse result through the front-end's surviving public surface, and the debug artifacts are still produced from within the driver's own run flow at the same two points (the token log after token formation, the parse log after parsing), without the driver doing work that now belongs elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the reporting duty was taken from the driver, so the driver's cooperation is the coupled change that makes the relocation real; leaving the driver calling dead hooks or moving its sequencing elsewhere would strand the cross-module contract the CLI and website rely on.

rubrics.criterion: No cross-module residue is left between the driver and the front-end: the driver does not pass report-related or debug arguments into a component that ignores them, both modules import only what they use, and no call references names that the repair removed or renamed.
rubrics.rationale: Because this case's change spans the front-end and its only caller, incomplete rewiring — an ignored debug flag threaded into a constructor that dropped it, or a call to a report method that no longer exists — is the specific coordination failure to catch, not a generic import-style issue.

rubrics.criterion: Each relocated duty ends up with exactly one live implementation: the repair leaves no parallel surviving copy of the correction lookup, the marker-rule check, or the report writing in the old idle owner 'for compatibility', so a future change to any of these duties has one place to edit.
rubrics.rationale: Split-brain ownership is the characteristic risk of redistributing this particular set of duties, since all of them already had a shared or original implementation to fall back on in this repository; keeping the old path alive would recreate the multi-reason-to-change problem the maintainer describes.

rubrics.criterion: The per-object machinery that the new ownership made unnecessary is deleted rather than bypassed: no seed/collect step for a correction dict, no dump-readiness flag or trace-path stem, no staged source fields, and no helper method servicing them survives reachable-but-unused in the refactored front-end.
rubrics.rationale: This instance injected a specific set of bookkeeping members whose only purpose was to hold the absorbed duties on one class; a repair that strands them as unreachable furniture keeps the exact reading burden the maintainer complained about, which is what this completion item measures.

rubrics.criterion: The repair leaves no dead imports or locals created by the move: the driver does not retain the AST-dump import or open-file locals that only served its old dump-writing blocks, and no module keeps an import that exclusively served code the repair removed.
rubrics.rationale: The moved reporting code carried its own import of the AST-dump facility and file-writing blocks in this instance, so their relocation predictably strands unused imports and locals — this concrete debris, not generic tidiness, is the cleanup this item grades.

rubrics.criterion: Token output is unchanged for any program source: the token codes, values, line numbers, and offsets produced for the language's keywords, operators, numbers, strings, and symbols are identical to before, including the multi-spelling aliases (nahin/nahi, bhayyo/bhaiyo, stretched mitroon-forms) mapping to the same tokens in the same order.
rubrics.rationale: The front-end that was restructured is the sole producer of this language's token stream; the alias-first correction behavior is the specific equivalence most at risk when vocabulary bookkeeping is relocated, and the maintainer explicitly pinned it as part of the contract.

rubrics.criterion: Program-boundary enforcement behavior is unchanged: a program missing the required opening word still fails with the language's starting error, a wrong, missing, or truncated closing phrase still fails with the same closing error, and well-formed programs still pass with the same tail-consuming check order.
rubrics.rationale: The marker-rule check is one of the duties relocated in this instance, and its error contract is observable by every user who miswrites a program, so the repair must preserve both the failure kinds and the truncation-sensitive check order.

rubrics.criterion: The debug evidence behavior is unchanged end to end: a debug-flagged run on a program file still writes the same two evidence files next to that program (token log and parse dump, same paths and same contents) at the same pipeline points, and inline-code sessions still write none.
rubrics.rationale: Because the report-writing duty moved in this instance, its trigger condition, path derivation, and content are the observable surface most likely to drift; the maintainer explicitly listed the evidence files, including that only filename runs produce them.

rubrics.criterion: Every in-repository consumer still runs against the repaired code without modification: the MODI command line (including its usage output and bad-argument exits), the website playground in both filename and inline-code modes, and the packaged example scripts, all behave as before via the driver's single public entry and the packaged exports under their existing names, with the front-end still constructible with its usual two positional arguments.
rubrics.rationale: This repository's import and call sites are pinned: the example gallery imports the packaged exports directly and the CLI and website go through the driver; the injected change deliberately preserved that boundary, so any repair that forces consumer edits or renames an export breaks the recorded behavior contract.

rubrics.criterion: The repair introduces no behavioral shortcuts while redistributing duties: corrections do not silently skip the alias tier or change its precedence for differently spelled words, reporting does not become mode-dependent in a new way (files appearing in inline sessions, or evidence dropped 'to stay safe'), and the marker check is not relaxed to best-effort — programs that used to fail must still fail the same way.
rubrics.rationale: Each of these plausible cheap shortcuts — flattening the correction cascade, gating reports differently to simplify the trigger, or lenient marker handling — would make the refactor look clean while quietly changing the language behavior this case was built to keep observationally identical.
